name: Dividend Arbitrage (Protected Dividend Capture)
summary: Buy 100 shares plus a deep ITM put before the ex-dividend date to collect the dividend with the share price risk hedged; the trade works only if the put's time value is less than the dividend, which the options market prices away.

legs.strike_rule: n/a — 100 shares bought no later than the session before the ex-dividend date
Deep ITM: strike >= spot x 1.05, delta <= -0.90, so the put's extrinsic value is minimal
legs.dte_rule: Nearest expiry AFTER the ex-dividend date, typically 7-21 DTE

max_profit: dividend_per_share x 100 - put_extrinsic x 100 - fees. Because the market prices puts to include the forthcoming dividend, this is almost always <= 0.
max_loss: put_extrinsic x 100 + fees + any assignment/slippage cost. Bounded, but reliably negative.

greeks.delta: +0.05 to +0.10 per unit (shares plus a -0.90+ delta put)
greeks.theta: negative — the put's remaining extrinsic decays

breakevens: Effectively: the trade profits only if dividend > put_extrinsic + fees.
when_to_use: Almost never, and the reason is structural: option pricing models already discount the known dividend out of the forward price, so a put spanning the ex-date is priced richer by approximately the dividend. The 'arbitrage' is a textbook exercise that the market closed decades ago. Include it in the bank as a recognisable pattern and a reject.
entry_rules: LEVEL 2/3 LEGAL: long stock plus long put, no short legs, fully permitted on Alpaca Level 3.
VIABILITY: negative expected value in essentially all cases. The gate below will almost never pass, which is the point.
Required test, evaluated at 15:00 ET the session before the ex-date: declared_dividend_per_share - (put_ask - max(0, put_strike - spot_ask)) - (fees/100) > $0.03 per share. Reject otherwise.
Dividend must be DECLARED (not estimated) with a confirmed ex-date, amount and record date.
Shares must settle in time to be holder of record: buy on or before the session immediately preceding the ex-date (T+1 settlement in 2026 means buying on the ex-date does NOT earn the dividend).
Never on a special dividend of more than 5% of the share price without checking for an OCC contract adjustment — adjusted contracts break every assumption in this trade.
management_rules: Hold exactly through the ex-date, then exit. This is not a position to hold.
If the put's extrinsic value rises above the dividend at any point before the ex-date, abandon the trade and close both legs.
Do not exercise the put on the ex-date reflexively: compare selling the put and selling the shares at market against exercising, and take the better of the two after fees.
Track the dividend receipt explicitly; the cash arrives on the payment date, not the ex-date, so the position's realised P/L is not final until then.
exit_rules: No short legs, therefore no assignment risk. Close both legs on the ex-date or the session after.
If the long put is ITM at 15:00 ET on its expiration day, close it rather than allowing auto-exercise, which would sell the shares at the strike without a decision.
Never carry this structure past the first expiry after the ex-date — its only purpose was the dividend.
If the dividend is cancelled or reduced after entry, close both legs the same session.
assignment_risk: NONE from short legs (there are none). The relevant mechanic is the mirror image: it is the counterparties to SHORT calls who get assigned around ex-dates, which is why an ITM call with extrinsic below the dividend is exercised. This strategy sits on the other side of that and therefore has no assignment exposure — only auto-exercise of the long put at expiry, which must be pre-empted by the 15:00 ET close rule.
buying_power: Full share cost (cash) or 50% Reg T margin plus the put debit; ~$10,000 or ~$5,000 plus the put on a $100 name, tied up for a dividend typically worth $50-$100.
liquidity_needs: Deep ITM puts are frequently wide-quoted and thinly traded — bid-ask on a deep ITM put of $0.15 wipes out a $0.50 dividend edge instantly. Require bid-ask <= $0.05 and OI >= 250 or skip.
common_mistakes: Believing the dividend is free money. Buying the shares on the ex-date instead of before it. Ignoring that the deep ITM put's spread is the real cost. Not checking for OCC contract adjustments on special dividends.
zero_dte_notes: Not applicable — the put must span the ex-date, so the tenor is set by the dividend calendar, not by DTE preference.
